changes: GET /api/v2/org/agent-permissions — removed the required property `results/defaults` from the response with the `200` status
GET /api/v2/org/agent-permissions — removed the required property `results/systemRoleMatrix` from the response with the `200` status
PUT /api/v2/org/agent-permissions — removed the required property `results/systemRoleMatrix` from the response with the `200` status
POST /api/v2/org/agent-permissions/reset — removed the required property `results/systemRoleMatrix` from the response with the `200` status

declaredAdvisories.reason: The per-role agent limits are removed. GET /api/v2/org/agent-permissions no longer returns results.defaults or results.systemRoleMatrix. PUT and POST /api/v2/org/agent-permissions/reset no longer return results.systemRoleMatrix. PUT no longer takes systemRoleMatrix; a request that still sends it gets no error and the server ignores it. The agent-identity feature flag is off by default on Cloud and on self-hosted instances and is set per organization. With the flag off, agent enforcement does not change. For organizations with the flag on and agent limits on, a person with a built-in role gets every agent capability that the organization setting allows, and per-role limits saved earlier no longer apply. The stored per-role rows stay in the database, unread and unchanged. During a rolling update an old settings page tab or an old UI pod reads the missing matrix and shows an error until refresh, and a save from the new page that reaches an old API pod is refused until the rollout ends. This is accepted because the settings page is the only client and a refresh or retry after the rollout fixes both.

impact.firstPartyOnly: The organization Agents settings page in the Lightdash web app is the only client of these operations, and it no longer reads or sends the per-role fields. An old tab of that page shows an error until refresh.
